children: Spillovers from South Korea's strong chip exports into domestic demand remain limited, Nomura economist Jeong Woo Park says. "So far, the clearest transmission has been through semiconductor facilities investment," he writes in a note. "Evidence of a broader improvement in employment, wages and household spending remains limited." Park expects private consumption growth to have slowed from the previous quarter in July-September. Higher interest rates are adding to household debt-servicing burdens, while the local stock market's selloff is eroding the consumption boost from household wealth, he says. Private-sector employment is also weakening, with September data showing further job losses in construction and slower job creation in services, he adds. Nomura expects the K-shaped divergence between economic sectors to persist longer than anticipated. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
